ko.executive_summary: Co-packaged optics (CPO) is driving a fundamental shift in optical interconnection architecture, with testing and validation moving upstream in the design cycle. Apple is actively hiring for silicon photonics expertise to implement light-based data links for server chip interconnects in data center applications.
key_facts: Keysight Technologies (NYSE: KEYS) is positioning for CPO testing workflow changes
Apple recruiting for silicon photonics and light-based server chip data links
Data center interconnection focus on optical (light-based) rather than electrical links

implications.text: CPO testing is shifting upstream, requiring earlier integration into the design flow rather than post-layout validation.
Apple's direct silicon photonics hiring signals hyperscalers are building in-house optical interconnect capabilities for competitive advantage.
Test vendors like Keysight must adapt instrumentation and workflows to support co-packaged architectures earlier in development cycles.
Migration from electrical to optical chip-to-chip links represents a fundamental shift in intra-rack and intra-node connectivity.

ko.counterpoint: Headline volume is limited and lacks specificity on technology milestones, timelines, or competitive player differentiation beyond Apple and Keysight.
